headline: WNBA Semifinals Game 2: Aces and Fever face must-win road tests as Liberty and Lynx eye 2-0 leads
whyCareReason: The entire season hangs in the balance for two-time defending champion Las Vegas and Caitlin Clark's Indiana Fever, with an 0-2 hole virtually guaranteeing elimination in WNBA postseason history.
teaser: Tuesday night across the WNBA: Barclays Center and Target Center host a blockbuster Game 2 double-header as Becky Hammon's Aces fight to square their heavyweight clash with New York, while Indiana seeks a statement road split in Minnesota.
story:
Why this one matters: Tuesday night presents the defining crucible of the 2026 WNBA postseason. In the unforgiving landscape of best-of-five playoff series, Game 2 is where seasons are preserved or pushed to the absolute brink.

At Barclays Center in Brooklyn, the Las Vegas Aces face unprecedented adversity. The two-time defending champions fell 87-77 in Sunday's opener as Breanna Stewart dominated both ends with 34 points and eight blocks. Aces coach Becky Hammon has emphasized ball protection after 18 costly turnovers in Game 1, demanding crisper ball movement around unanimous MVP A'ja Wilson to prevent Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones from feasting in transition.

Two hours later at Target Center, the Indiana Fever look to strike back against the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx. Napheesa Collier's 28-point masterclass secured an 88-82 win for Minnesota in Game 1, but Caitlin Clark's fourth-quarter surge (14 points) provided the Fever with a proven blueprint. If Indiana can knock down perimeter jumpers early and control defensive rebounds, they have a golden opportunity to steal home-court advantage before the series heads to Indianapolis.
stakes: Championship series leverage: teams leading 2-0 in best-of-five WNBA history have advanced in 24 of 25 all-time series (96 percent).
rivalryAngle: New York is hungry for sweet revenge after falling to Las Vegas in the 2023 Finals, while Clark and Collier continue to produce box-office postseason drama.
